---
title: "Tutorial 2: coordinate four rounding decisions"
description: "A rank-one example cancels error that independent rounding leaves positive."
---

## Problem

Four values lie halfway between adjacent grid points. Independent Bernoulli
rounding has positive expected product error. Because all four sensitivities
point in the same direction, two up and two down decisions can cancel exactly.

```python
import numpy as np

from experiments.discrepancy import (
    conditional_expectation_finish,
    enumerate_binary_optimum,
    null_space_reduce,
    same_grid_bernoulli_energy,
)

block = np.ones((4, 1))
theta = np.full(4, 0.5)

_, exact_error = enumerate_binary_optimum(block, theta)
relaxed, trace = null_space_reduce(block, theta)
rounded, _ = conditional_expectation_finish(block, theta, relaxed)
coordinated_error = float(np.linalg.norm((rounded - theta) @ block) ** 2)

print(same_grid_bernoulli_energy(block, theta))
print(trace["residual_size"], rounded.astype(int).tolist())
print(coordinated_error, exact_error)

assert coordinated_error == exact_error == 0.0
```

The independent reference is `1.0`; the coordinated error is `0.0`. Any vector
with two zeros and two ones has the same cancellation.

## Boundary

This example uses a rank-one block and unconstrained midpoint residues. The full
protocol separately tests higher rank, row-sensitivity imbalance, fixed offsets,
and a reusable static setting.
